lesson_title: How Long Until It Doubles: Growth and Decay
hook_text: A dealer's van dropped from R320 000 to R135 000 in three years. What percentage did it REALLY lose per year? Hint: it is not the total divided by three.
clip_script: A delivery van: 320 000 rand new, three years later it is worth 135 000. What did it shed per year? Do NOT divide the loss by three — percentages multiply, they never split evenly. Detective method: divide end by start — 0,421875 of the value kept. That happened as one mystery factor, multiplied by itself three times. Un-multiply with the cube root: 0,75. The van kept three quarters of itself each year — it shed twenty-five percent per annum, on a shrinking base, which is why the total loss looks nothing like three equal bites. Now flip the question: how long until money DOUBLES at 7,5 percent? The unknown hides in the exponent, and only the logarithm can fetch it down: log 2 over log 1,075 — 9,58. But banks pay at year ends, so the money actually crosses double when year ten's interest lands. Divide, root, log, round to the calendar — four moves, and every growth and decay question in existence opens.
visual_style: A shrinking van sliding down a curved ramp with yearly factor labels of 0,75, then a money escalator climbing toward a DOUBLE line with the logarithm pulling n down from the exponent.
pacing: A hook on the wrong answer, a beat on the cube root reveal, brisk through the logarithm, decisive close on the calendar rounding.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and un-multiply any percentage the world throws at you.
